children.title: Administration cancels about $400 million in Columbia grants and contracts
children.description_medium: On March 7, 2025, the administration canceled about $400 million in federal grants and contracts to Columbia University, citing what it described as the university’s failure to address antisemitic harassment. This was a specified funding action involving grants and contracts, not a verified halt to every form of federal support.
children.description_long: The Trump administration canceled about $400 million in federal grants and contracts to Columbia University on March 7, 2025, Reuters reported. The administration cited what it described as Columbia’s failure to address antisemitic harassment. The reported action applied to a specified amount of grants and contracts; the supplied source does not establish that every form of federal funding or educational support to Columbia was suspended. Columbia faced a separate administrative process from Harvard, whose grant and contract funding was frozen in April after the university rejected a list of demands. The March Columbia action therefore should not be combined with the later Harvard funding freeze or represented as an August blanket action against multiple universities. Reuters later reported Columbia reached an agreement with the government in July and regained most suspended funding; that later development is separate from the March cancellation described here. The evidence in this packet supports the amount, date, institution, and stated rationale reported at the time, while not establishing the broader claim that Yale and other universities were included in the same action.
children.date_uncertainty: March 7 is the Reuters publication date and the reported date of the grant and contract cancellations.

children.title: Administration freezes about $2.3 billion in Harvard grants and contracts
children.description_medium: On April 14, 2025, the administration froze about $2.2 billion in Harvard grants and $60 million in contract value after Harvard rejected administration demands concerning campus governance, antisemitism, DEI and other policies. The action followed a separate process from Columbia’s March funding cancellations. Reuters reported these values separately.
children.description_long: The Trump administration froze approximately $2.2 billion in grants and $60 million in contract value for Harvard University after the university rejected administration demands concerning campus governance, antisemitism, diversity policies and other matters, Reuters reported on April 14, 2025. The combined grant and contract amounts total about $2.3 billion. This was a distinct funding action from the March 7 cancellation of about $400 million in Columbia grants and contracts, involving a different institution, date and administrative process. The supplied reporting supports the scale of the freeze and the immediate context of Harvard’s rejection of the demands. It does not establish that all federal education and research funding to Harvard was permanently suspended or that the same action applied to Yale. The original account placed the Columbia and Harvard events together in August and described a blanket freeze to three universities, which is not supported by these sources. This record reports the specific Harvard grant and contract freeze and keeps its reported scope separate from the Columbia action.
children.date_uncertainty: April 14 is the Reuters publication date and the reported date of the funding freeze.

unresolved_components.title: Yale funding suspension and blanket three-university August action
unresolved_components.reason: The packet says no comparable blanket Yale funding suspension was verified and identifies the Columbia and Harvard actions as separate.
unresolved_components.missing_evidence: Dated records showing a comparable Yale action or one August decision suspending all federal education and research funding to Harvard, Yale and Columbia.

rationale: The supplied Reuters sources support separate, specified Columbia and Harvard funding actions in March and April 2025. The unsupported August three-university blanket claim is left unresolved.
